configs.description: The chassis with two AC supplies and two fan modules fitted, front-to-rear air, before any part number: the shape every build below starts from.
configs.name: base

configs.description: Two DC supplies and front-to-rear air: PWR-511-DC-RED supplies and FAN-7011M-F fan modules. The data sheet lists no DC part number for the switch; the supplies are spares, and a DC build is ordered through the "#" configurable SKUs.
configs.name: dc-f

configs.description: Two DC supplies and rear-to-front air: PWR-511-DC-BLUE supplies and FAN-7011M-R fan modules. No DC part number is listed for the switch.
configs.name: dc-r

configs.description: The 7280SR3-48YC8 with two AC supplies and front-to-rear air: PWR-511-AC-RED supplies and FAN-7011M-F fan modules, all with red handles. Ordered as DCS-7280SR3-48YC8-F.
configs.name: f

configs.description: The 7280SR3K-48YC8A, the K build with an eight-core CPU, with front-to-rear air. It draws 162 W typical and 338 W maximum (guide Table 4), against 155 W and 325 W for the other builds. Ordered as DCS-7280SR3K-48YC8A-F.
configs.name: k-a-f

configs.description: The 7280SR3K-48YC8A with rear-to-front air, drawing 162 W typical and 338 W maximum. Ordered as DCS-7280SR3K-48YC8A-R.
configs.name: k-a-r

configs.description: The 7280SR3K-48YC8, the same hardware with 64 GB of memory, an SSD and the large-routes licence, with front-to-rear air. Ordered as DCS-7280SR3K-48YC8-F.
configs.name: k-f

configs.description: The 7280SR3K-48YC8 with rear-to-front air. Ordered as DCS-7280SR3K-48YC8-R.
configs.name: k-r

configs.description: The 7280SR3-48YC8 with two AC supplies and rear-to-front air: PWR-511-AC-BLUE supplies and FAN-7011M-R fan modules, all with blue handles. Ordered as DCS-7280SR3-48YC8-R.
configs.name: r

gaps.note: Typical / maximum power 155 W / 325 W (guide Table 4) against 154 W / 324 W (data sheet) for the 7280SR3-48YC8 and 7280SR3K-48YC8. The two documents agree for the 7280SR3K-48YC8A. The guide's figures are used.
gaps.wanted: the maker's statement of which is current.

gaps.note: The 7280SR3K-48YC8A draws 162 W typical and 338 W maximum (guide Table 4) against 155 W and 325 W for the other two, has an eight-core CPU in place of a quad-core, and the K builds carry 64 GB of memory against 8 GB. No configuration can state a device attribute (the same open gap as cisco/asr-9001). The attrs carry the 7280SR3-48YC8's figures and the platform lines name all three.

Storage temperature -25 to 70 C (guide Table 2) against -40 to 70 C (data sheet), and relative humidity 5 to 90 percent against 5 to 95 percent. The guide's, the older document by three months, are in attrs.
gaps.wanted: the maker's statement of which is current.

gaps.note: The guide's Figures 3-1 to 3-4 are isometric drawings of another switch and carry no measure, and the kit guides for KIT-7001, KIT-7101 and the other spares are not held, so no ear position or rail kit is written.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned drawing of the mounting bracket position, and the kit guides.

gaps.note: Figure C-6 draws four dots a QSFP port, but Table 10 describes one port LED and does not say what each of the four shows. All four are given Table 10's states.
gaps.wanted: the guide's account of the port lamps, or a photograph of the lit face.

gaps.note: Figure C-6 draws two lamps under each SFP column. Which belongs to the upper port and which to the lower is not stated; the odd port is given the left lamp.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the lit face.

gaps.note: The speed bands' legends, the small print over the cages, the system and fan lamp glyphs and the PS1 and PS2 legends are unreadable or barely readable in the 552 px figure. The glyphs and the two PS legends are drawn as read; the band and cage legends are not drawn.
Which side the latches of the stacked cages face is not visible in the figure. The library's belly-to-belly convention is used (upper cage upright, lower turned 180).
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the stacked cages.

gaps.note: The management block's arrow marks and its console symbol are drawn as the 7280CR3-32D4 draws them; the order of the three ports follows the datasheet's rear view and the library's other Arista stacks, and the figure's 1.25 px/mm resolves it only as three stacked ports.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the rear management block.

gaps.note: The PWR-511-DC supplies are drawn as the AC supply's housing with a plain two-pole terminal block. The guide shows a DC supply only in isometric figures; the real terminal arrangement is not drawn.
gaps.wanted: a flat drawing or photograph of the PWR-511-DC.

gaps.note: The guide's power tables and the data sheet give whole-switch figures only; the fan modules' missing power figure (lint L27) stands. The supplies state their output.
The 1RU grounding point is on the bottom of the chassis for KIT-GND-EXT-1RU (guide section 4.2, Table 5, Figure 4-2). No flat figure measures it, so it is not placed.
gaps.wanted: a flat drawing of the bottom with the grounding bracket holes.

chassis.note: Guide Table 1: 48.3 x 4.4 x 46.7 cm (19 x 1.75 x 18.4 in), 9.2 kg (20.2 lbs), the same for the 7280SR3-48YC8, 7280SR3K-48YC8 and 7280SR3K-48YC8A. Data sheet: 43.99 x 4.35 x 46.7 cm (17.3 x 1.72 x 18.38 in), 20.2 lbs (9.18 kg). The width: 48.3 cm is over the mounting ears, so the body between them, which is what is modelled, is the data sheet's 43.99 cm (440.0 here), a 21.5 mm ear each side. THE HEIGHT IS THE DATA SHEET'S 43.5 (4.35 cm), not the 43.7 of the other 1RU 7280R3 models; the guide rounds every model to 4.4 cm. The depth is the data sheet's 467.0 (the guide's 46.7 cm). 1RU.

colour.note: The front plate is the 7280CR3-32D4's #aaabad, read there as the median of bare-plate pixels in the guide's figure of the same family.

configurations.note: Data sheet ordering information: DCS-7280SR3-48YC8-F and -R, DCS-7280SR3K-48YC8-F and -R, and DCS-7280SR3K-48YC8A-F and -R ("front to rear air, 2 x AC" and "rear to front air, 2 x AC"). The "#" SKUs ("configurable fans and psu") are orders of parts, not part numbers a DCIM can hold, and are not listed. The data sheet lists no DC build of the switch: the PWR-511-DC-RED and -BLUE supplies are spares, so the DC configurations are examples with no part number. The K and K-A builds share the base model's size, weight, figure and supplies and differ in memory, CPU, SSD and routes (and, for the A, power draw), which a configuration cannot state; each is a configuration with its own part numbers. There is no empty-bay (-S) configuration: no -S suffix exists in this family and the guide draws no blank for a power supply or fan module.

ears.note: NOT MODELLED. The guide's Chapter 3 mounts the switch with the accessory-kit brackets and shows them in isometric drawings of a different switch ("Illustrations in this chapter depict the mounting of a DCS-7050QX-32S switch") that carry no measure. The data sheet lists the spares KIT-7001, KIT-2POST-1U-NT, KIT-4POST-NT, KIT-7001-4POST-L, KIT-7101, KIT-7101-RK, KIT-7101-LD-RK, KIT-ADJ-RLR and KIT-GND-EXT-1RU. No figure measures a bracket position, and the kit guides are not held, so no ear position is written and no rail kit is listed in chassis.kits. Recorded in the gap rack-ears.

environment.note: Guide Table 2: operating 0 to 40 C, storage -25 to 70 C, altitude 0 to 3,000 m, humidity 5 to 90 percent non-condensing. Data sheet: operating 0 to 40 C, storage -40 to 70 C, humidity 5 to 95 percent, altitude 0 to 3,000 m. Storage temperature and humidity differ: gap `environment`, the guide's used.

front-legend.note: The model legend reads "7280SR3-48YC8" under the maker's wordmark at the top left (read at 552 px; the print is small). THE WORDMARK IS NOT DRAWN: a logo-zone region is reserved over it and the plain model text is set. The text is as the guide's caption names the model.

front-ports.note: Figure C-6 at 1.2545 px/mm. Forty-eight SFP cages in two stacked rows (ports 1 to 48), twelve columns on each side of the QSFP block, in groups of six columns: the tab centres of ports 1, 3, ... 11 read 11.4, 25.9, ... on a 14.25 mm pitch (the registry's ganged-SFP pitch, whose cages abut) with a 2.5 mm gap between the groups of six; ports 25 to 47 start 260.0 mm from the left. Eight QSFP100 cages in two stacked rows of four columns (49 to 56), centred 190.7, 209.6, 228.6 and 247.4 mm, a 19.0 mm pitch. The rows read from the tabs at 18.1 and 31.9 mm down, a row pitch of 13.8. The belly-to-belly orientation is the library's convention (upper cage upright, lower turned 180); the figure is too small to show the latch side.

fru-bays.note: Guide Appendix E (E.2 power supplies, E.3 fan modules) gives removal and installation procedures, and the data sheet calls the supplies "1+1 hot-swappable" and the fans "hot-swap". SO THE TWO POWER SUPPLIES AND THE TWO FAN MODULES ARE BAYS. Nothing on this chassis is a built-in unit. The management block, the USB port and the console port are part of the chassis and are placements.

gate-1-front.note: Figure C-6 passes. The raster is 552 x 137 pixels; the body measures 552 px wide and 55 px tall (aspect 10.0), against the data sheet's 440.0 / 43.5 = 10.1, so the figure is near-orthographic and carries geometry at 1.2545 px/mm (the 440 mm body is the scale anchor, its left edge read at 1 px). One pixel is 0.8 mm, so every position is good to about 0.8 mm, and every one is `estimated` because it is read off a picture and no dimension states it. The old guide's Figure 52 is the same 552 x 137 raster, compared pixel for pixel (no pixel differs), so it is a repeat of the source and not a second reading. The cages were read from the white port-number tabs in an eight-times enlargement.

gate-1-rear.note: Figure D-1 is a 553 x 141 px raster whose chassis is 551 px between its edges and 54 px tall (aspect 10.2 against 10.1), 1.252 px/mm over the 440 mm body; positions are good to about 0.8 mm. The guide draws the rear generically (D-1 to D-4) and does not say which model uses which. The 7280SR3-48YC8 is mapped to D-1 by its two fan modules (data sheet: "Hot-swappable Fans 2 (1+1 redundant)"), its 1RU height, its two power supplies and its management ports at the rear (Figure C-6 has none at the front). THE MAPPING IS ESTIMATED.

interface-names.note: Not printed and not modelled. EOS names ports Ethernet1 to Ethernet56 and Management1; this is the vendor's convention and no held document prints it.

lifecycle.note: Searched 2026-10-23 (web searches of Arista's end-of-sale notices). Notice 23789, "End of Sale of the Arista DCS-7280SR3K-48YC8 Series" (https://www.arista.com/en/support/advisories-notices/end-of-sale/23789-end-of-sale-of-the-arista-dcs-7280sr3k-48yc8-series), announced April 10, 2026, covers the SKUs -F, -R, # and -F-DC of the 7280SR3K-48YC8, with the last date to order October 10, 2026, end of life October 10, 2031, and the 7280SR3K-48YC8A as the suggested replacement. It names neither the 7280SR3-48YC8 nor the 7280SR3K-48YC8A, and no notice for those was found, so the device records the announcement and this note says which build it covers: the K builds (k-f and k-r) only.

other-faces.note: No source draws the top, bottom or sides flat. The guide's installation figures are isometric. Each carries an `empty` sentence. The 1RU grounding point is on the bottom of the chassis (guide section 4.2, Table 5, KIT-GND-EXT-1RU); no figure measures it.

port-lamps.note: Guide Appendix A.1.2, Table 10 and Figure C-6 callout 6, "Port status LED (port 25)": each SFP column has two green lamps in the strip under the lower row, 5.8 mm apart and centred on the column; they are modelled as one lamp for each port of the column, the odd port's on the left. Each QSFP column has a group of four lamps above the upper cage and four below the lower one, 4.0 mm apart: four lamps a QSFP port are modelled. Table 10 gives one set of states, so every lamp carries it; what each of four means is the gap port-lamp-count, and which of the two SFP lamps names which port is the gap sfp-lamp-pairing.

port-numbering.note: Figure C-6 (callout 1, "Port numbers") prints 1 over 2, 3 over 4, and so on, 1 to 48 across the SFP columns and 49 over 50 to 55 over 56 across the QSFP columns, which sit between ports 24 and 25 in space and are numbered after 48. The odd number is the upper cage. The figure prints each number on a white tab over the cage opening; a seated cage hides what is painted under it, so the numerals are set in the band between the two rows, the odd number left of its column centre and the even one right of it. EOS interface names are not printed on the metal and are not modelled.

power.note: Guide Table 4: typical / maximum 155 W / 325 W for the 7280SR3-48YC8 and 7280SR3K-48YC8, and 162 W / 338 W for the 7280SR3K-48YC8A, each with PWR-511-AC or PWR-511-DC. The data sheet gives 154 W / 324 W for the first two and 162 W / 338 W for the A (gap `size-conflict`); the guide's figures are used and the typical is "measured at 25C ambient with 50% load on all ports". A configuration cannot state a device attribute, so the device carries 155 W / 325 W and the -48YC8A figure is in the gap config-scoped-device-attrs and in the description of its configurations.

rear.note: Figure D-1 at 1.252 px/mm, the rear seen from behind with x = 0 at the left of the drawing. PS1 is the left and PS2 the right (callouts 1 and 6). Each power supply module is 73.5 mm wide (the data sheet's "73.5MM") at 4.4 and 361.5 mm across and 1.85 mm down. The management block is a grey plate 82.5 to 100.5 mm across with the Ethernet management port, the USB port and the RJ-45 console port stacked in it, in the order the library draws other Arista management stacks. Two fan modules 78.6 mm wide at 105.7 and 276.6 mm across and 2.55 mm down. Between the fans is a grey plate printed with ASSY NUMBER, SERIAL NUMBER and MAC ADDRESS fields and, under them, PS1 and PS2 legends beside airflow arrows (the arrows are not drawn).

rear-fan.note: Data sheet: "Hot-swappable Fans 2 (N+1 redundant)", "Fan Tray FAN-7011M" and the spares FAN-7011M-F (front-to-rear) and FAN-7011M-R (rear-to-front). Guide section 2.1: a red handle is an air-exit module and a blue handle an air-inlet one, and every module must have the same direction. The two fan modules are bays that accept FAN-7011M-F or -R; the -R configurations seat the blue modules.

sources.note: 7280R3 Series Quick Start Guide, Arista Networks, document DOC-07041-01, 63 pages, PDF created 2025-05-16 (https://www.arista.com/assets/data/pdf/qsg/qsg-books/QS_7280R3.pdf): Table 1 (dimensions and weights), Table 2 (operating and storage), Table 3 (power input), Table 4 (power draw and supported supplies), section 2.1 (airflow orientation, handle colour), Table 5 (grounding), section 4.5 (serial and management cables), Appendix A (status indicators, Tables 9 to 13), Appendix C (Figure C-6, the front panel of the DCS-7280SR3-48YC8, 7280SR3K-48YC8 and 7280SR3K-48YC8A), Appendix D (Figure D-1, the rear panel with two fan modules), Appendix E (field replacement). 7280 Data Center Switches Quick Start Guide, Arista Networks, 58 pages, PDF created 2022-06-03 (https://www.arista.com/assets/data/pdf/qsg/qsg-books/QS_7280_1RU_Gen3.pdf): Figure 52 (DCS-7280SR3-48YC8 and 7280SR3K-48YC8), the cross-check of Figure C-6. 7280R3 Series Data Center Switch Router Data Sheet, Arista Networks, 03-0045-59, dated August 11th, 2025 (https://www.arista.com/assets/data/pdf/Datasheets/7280R3-Data-Sheet.pdf): the model comparison of the 7280SR3-48YC8, SR3K-48YC8 and SR3K-48YC8A, the power supply specifications and the ordering information. Held and checked first: intake COVERAGE.md and SOURCES.md, which list no photograph, Visio stencil, 3D model or CAD file for this model (Arista publishes none; the stencil zip could not be fetched). The data sheet's picture of the face is a thumbnail. No drawing, photograph or logo is copied into the library, only transcribed facts and new drawings.

speed-strips.note: Guide Figure C-6: a cyan band between the two rows under each group of six SFP columns and a lavender band under the QSFP block, with tiny legends. The bands are drawn in those colours at 23.9 to 25.9 mm down; the legends are unreadable and are not drawn. Two brass-coloured screw heads sit at the ends of the QSFP lamp strip.

status-lamps.note: Guide Appendix A.1.1, Table 9 and Figure C-6 callouts 2 to 5: a system status lamp (blinking green on power-up, green normal, blue locator, amber for two or more failed fans), a fan status lamp (green, amber for one module removed or failed, red for two or more) and a status lamp for each of the two power supplies (green operating, off removed or faulty). Four lamps in a row at 420.1, 423.8, 427.9 and 432.1 mm and 6.2 mm down, with a symbol or legend above each: a circled mark, a fan, and two legends read as PS1 and PS2.

vents.note: The figure shows a perforated grid along the top (1.2 to 11.6 mm down) in four fields, with solid strips at 87 to 93 mm and over the QSFP block, and a row of tiny holes along the bottom lip (about 42 mm down). Each field is drawn in its measured extent; the individual squares are not drawn one by one.
